title: HYDRO-GUARD AI — Phase 1 Copernicus DEM GLO-30 Elevation Audit
scientific_constraints_statement: 1. Copernicus DEM GLO-30 is a Digital Surface Model (DSM) capturing top-of-canopy and rooftop surfaces, not submerged riverbeds or pipe inverts.
2. DEM endpoint differences establish surface elevation trends only; they do not establish physically validated hydraulic flow paths.
3. Hydraulic direction status is classified as UNVERIFIED across edges pending ground-truth surveyed channel-bed or pipe invert data.
4. Assumed elevations from config.py are strictly preserved; DEM surface elevations are maintained in dedicated attributes.

5. The +14m to +25m offset between assumed and DEM elevations is documented as an empirical difference; hypotheses regarding geodetic datum or DSM bias remain unverified without independent ground benchmarks.
6. Existing graph topology, edge identifiers, and API compatibility are fully preserved.

elevation_delta_analysis.verified_fact: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM (EGM2008 datum) is 19.61m higher than the assumed value (560.0m). Original assumed values in config.py lack recorded geodetic datum or benchmark metadata.
possible_unverified_explanations: Potential geoid/vertical datum offset between local Survey of India MSL benchmark and EGM2008 geoid (unverified without official SOI benchmark data).

discrepancy_notes: Assumed model has negative/reverse slope (-4.0m drop). Original config assigned downstream node higher elevation than upstream node.

Copernicus surface DSM indicates reverse elevation difference (-4.15m). CAUTION: Urban surface features (buildings/flyovers) or localized backwater conditions may mask underlying canal/pipe invert slope.
edges_hydraulic_validation.special_investigation_note: RAMBAGH-TO-RAJWADA INVESTIGATION: In the assumed model, Rambagh (536m) is set 4m lower than Rajwada (540m), producing an unphysical assumed negative drop of -4.0m. In the real Copernicus DEM, authoritative bilinear sampling yields Rajwada at 556.41m and Rambagh at 552.26m (surface delta: -4.15m; nearest-neighbor cell center was 551.99m). Geographic investigation reveals Rajwada is in the dense historic commercial center (palace/commercial rooftops), whereas Rambagh is at the natural river embankment. Surface DEM cannot see underground pipe/channel inverts. Per scientific constraints, existing edge direction is strictly preserved and marked UNVERIFIED until municipal invert records are available.

remaining_uncertainties: Underground sewer and stormwater pipe invert levels are unmeasured in satellite DEM data.
Copernicus GLO-30 measures surface reflections (rooftops/canopy) rather than bare-earth riverbed inverts.
Rambagh to Rajwada exhibits adverse surface elevation difference (-4.15m), likely influenced by commercial rooftops at Rajwada bazaar, but subsurface invert levels are unverified.
The +14m to +25m elevation offset between assumed and DEM values cannot be conclusively attributed to EGM2008 datum shift or DSM bias without official Survey of India benchmark calibration sheets.
Dynamic hydrodynamic flow, backwater surcharging, and head losses during peak monsoon require calibrated 1D/2D hydraulic modeling.
